text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply all safe changes immediately, then log the rest for review.

This keeps improvement moving without waiting for human checks, which speeds up gains. Trade-off: we risk applying a change that later fails a deeper review, but the static analysis and regression checks already filter out the obvious bad ones.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t bad changes slipping through—it’s that "safe" is subjective until proven by failure. Auto-applying based on static analysis alone assumes no blind spots in the checks, which regression tests won’t catch if the test suite itself is flawed. Settle it by running a controlled experiment: auto-apply only changes that pass *both* static analysis *and* a new, minimal regression suite for 48 hours, then compare failure rates against manual review.
